title: Java Method Overloading
learningObjectives: Define method overloading as multiple methods sharing a name with different parameter lists.
Identify valid overloads using parameter count, types or order.
Explain why return type alone cannot distinguish overloaded methods.
Predict which overload is selected for a given argument list.
Use overloading when related operations need a consistent method name.

understand.concept: Method overloading allows a class to declare multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists. The compiler selects an applicable overload using the arguments supplied. Changing only the return type does not create a valid overload.
understand.whyItMatters: Overloading gives related operations a consistent name while allowing them to accept different kinds or amounts of input, such as calculating a total from two or three values.
understand.analogy: Think of a method as a named tool: give it the information it needs, let it perform one defined task, and use its result when appropriate.
understand.analogyLimit: A program follows exact language rules; a real-world tool may need judgment and safety checks that code must model explicitly.

explain.narrative:
## Valid overloads

Methods can be overloaded by changing the number of parameters, their types, or their order. Each overload must have a distinct parameter signature.

## Return type is not enough

Two methods cannot be overloaded by changing only their return type. A call does not include a return-type selection, so the compiler would not have a unique signature to use.

## Choosing an overload

The compiler resolves a call from its argument count, types and applicable conversions. Ambiguous calls are compile-time errors.

## Common mistakes

- Declaring two methods with identical parameter types and order.
- Assuming a different return type makes a distinct overload.
- Forgetting that argument order can affect overload selection.
- Creating overloads whose calls become ambiguous.

questions.prompt: What makes two methods valid overloads?
questions.answer: They have the same name and different parameter lists
options: They have the same name and different parameter lists
They have different return types only
questions.explanation: Overloading is distinguished by the parameter signature.

questions.prompt: Can methods be overloaded by changing only the return type?
questions.explanation: The return type is not part of the method signature used for overload selection.

questions.prompt: Which is a valid overload pair?
questions.answer: sum(int, int) and sum(int, int, int)
options: sum(int, int) and sum(int, int, int)
sum(int) and sum(int) with different return types
questions.explanation: The pair differs in parameter count.

questions.prompt: What information is used to select an overloaded method?
questions.answer: The supplied argument list and applicable conversions
options: The supplied argument list and applicable conversions
questions.explanation: The compiler resolves calls using argument count, types and conversions.
